observations: Photo 0 shows a used inline 4-cylinder car engine sitting on pavement, engine bay/wiring harness still attached, removed from a vehicle.
Green paint marks are visible on the valve cover and intake area, a common marking used by used-parts dealers (often to signal 'tested' or lot number), not a manufacturer mark.
A watermark/logo is visible in the corner of the photo but it is the seller's own stamp, not a part identifier.
No engine code, casting number, VIN tag, or brand nameplate is legible anywhere on the block, head, or intake manifold.
A person's legs/feet and sandals are visible in the background, confirming an outdoor open-yard setting typical of Lagos spare-parts markets.
No odometer, dashboard, or import/customs document is shown to support mileage or origin claims.
No video or audio is provided to support 'tested and working, no knock' claim.

claims.evidence: No Korean brand badge, sticker, or casting mark visible in photo 0.
No import tag, customs sticker, or shipping document shown.
No start-up video, compression test, or diagnostic readout provided.
Cannot be judged from a still photo; requires audio/video of running engine.
No odometer or mileage sticker shown.
Valve cover bolts appear intact in photo 0 but torque marks/seal paint are not visible or detailed enough to confirm the block or head was never opened.

risks.risk: Engine make, model, and displacement are unreadable, which determines vehicle compatibility and base price tier.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code sticker/plate (usually on block near timing cover or on intake manifold) or casting number stamped into the block.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all without this, since compatible-vehicle price tiers differ drastically

risks.risk: Internal mechanical condition (knock, compression, timing chain wear) cannot be assessed from a static photo.
risks.proof: Video of the engine running with audible idle and revs, plus a compression test reading.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / needs rebuild

risks.risk: Claimed low mileage cannot be confirmed.
risks.proof: Photo of odometer or original import mileage sticker/manifest.

risks.risk: Claimed Belgian/Korean origin (affects trust in 'tokunbo' grading) is unverifiable.
risks.proof: Photo of shipping container papers, customs duty receipt, or Belgian de-registration document.

risks.risk: Hidden damage such as cracked block, stripped threads, or missing sensors/wiring not visible from this single angle.
risks.proof: Additional photos from all sides including underside/oil pan and close-ups of connector plugs.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code/ID plate or stamped casting number to identify make, model, and displacement.
Video of the engine running (with sound) to support 'tested, no knock' claim.
Photo of odometer reading or original mileage documentation.
Photos from additional angles (rear, underside, both sides) to check for cracks, missing parts, or oil leaks.
Any import/customs paperwork supporting the Belgium/Tokunbo claim.
response.reason: The engine's make, model, and displacement -- which are the primary drivers of price for a used engine -- are not legible in the single photo provided, and the seller's working/mileage/origin claims cannot be judged from a static image alone.
